description: Homes are linked by an undirected 8-nearest-neighbor graph limited to a 5 km haversine radius, with cosine-similarity weights and any similarity below 0 dropped; API neighbors are the query's one-way matches under that rule and use edge type combined.
target_note: Natural log of USD sale price. USD = exp(log_price).

graph_rule.symmetrization: One-way kNN is symmetrized: an undirected edge is kept when either endpoint lists the other. Mutual kNN is not required.
graph_rule.similarity_floor_note: Edges with cosine similarity below 0 are dropped.
graph_rule.api_edge_type_note: A returned neighbor is inside 5 km and weighted by feature cosine similarity, so edge_type is combined.
graph_rule.request_neighbors: One-way k nearest existing homes from the query that pass the radius and the similarity floor, excluding the query property id.
graph_rule.training: The static graph includes every home. Loss is mean squared error on train indices only; validation indices are used for early stopping; test indices are reported separately.
graph_rule.zipcode: zipcode in the 18-vector is the raw ZIP integer from kc_cleaned_data.csv. It is standardized with the training-split mean and standard deviation before cosine weights and message passing. The other 17 inputs are used as stored.

provenance.loss: mse on train indices only; static graph over all homes
provenance.coordinates: raw lat/long from data/kc_house_data.csv joined by row-aligned id
provenance.features: data/kc_cleaned_data.csv in FEATURE_ORDER; zipcode standardized on the train split
provenance.comparison_note: Test metrics describe this GNN only. They are not a claim to beat XGBoost.
